_comment: SHAPE EXAMPLE ONLY — do not publish verbatim. This is the BUILD/ARCHITECT template the ask-project skill points to: when a coding agent is asked to BUILD or ARCHITECT a project, its architecture thinking should decompose into a question per consequential decision across the coverage dimensions and yield ~12-25 deduplicated questions (about 5 horizon:"now" blockers + the rest next/later). This set is tailored to a sample build — "a team scheduling SaaS" — spanning purpose, audience, success, scope, stack/framework, data model, auth/identity, hosting/deploy, payments, API shape, state mgmt, realtime, performance, testing, accessibility, ai_behavior, economics, distribution, maintenance. INSPECT the real repo and TAILOR to the actual project; drop any question the code or the user's instructions already answer; re-publish new batches as new decision points surface. Publish with: node bin/ask.mjs ask --file <your-tailored-file>.json

questions.title: In one sentence, what is the single scheduling problem this product must solve better than a shared calendar?
questions.context: The whole architecture orients around this. Pinning it now stops the build drifting into a generic calendar clone.
questions.consequence: Determines the core domain model (shifts vs meetings vs bookings) and which flows we build first.

questions.title: Who schedules first — the team manager, the individual member, or an external customer booking time?
questions.context: Audience drives the default view, permissions, and onboarding. Each implies a very different first screen.
questions.consequence: Shapes the role model, the landing surface, and whether we need a public booking page in v1.

options.label: Team manager assigning people to slots
External customer booking a team member

questions.title: What one measurable outcome in 90 days tells us the scheduling product is working?
questions.context: A single success metric keeps the roadmap honest (e.g. 'teams publish a full week in under 5 min').
questions.consequence: Decides what we instrument, what the dashboard surfaces, and how we prioritize polish.

questions.title: Which capabilities are in scope for the FIRST usable release?
questions.context: Cutting v1 to the essential scheduling path ships value sooner and de-risks the rest.
questions.consequence: Everything unchecked moves to a later milestone; checked items become the build plan now.

options.label: Shift swap / trade requests with approval
Public booking page for external guests

questions.recommendation: Recommended: shared calendar + availability + reminders for v1; defer public booking and reporting unless they are the point.

questions.title: What frontend stack should the scheduling UI be built on?
questions.context: A calendar-heavy, multi-role app is a long-lived application, not a brochure site — the stack choice compounds.
questions.consequence: Sets the component model, state approach, SSR story, and how fast the team can add views.

options.label: No preference — recommend the best fit

questions.recommendation: Recommended: Angular if this grows into a multi-role, many-view operations tool; React+Vite if it stays a focused SPA.

questions.title: How should recurring availability and booked slots be modeled?
questions.context: The recurrence/exception model is the hardest near-irreversible choice in a scheduler; getting it wrong forces a migration.
questions.consequence: Determines query complexity for 'who is free when', timezone handling, and conflict detection.

options.label: Hybrid — rules for templates, materialized for booked

questions.recommendation: Recommended: hybrid — store availability as recurrence templates, materialize concrete slots when booked.

questions.title: Where should the primary scheduling data live?
questions.context: The datastore is a near-irreversible choice; picking it early avoids a painful migration under load.
questions.consequence: Determines the ORM, timezone/temporal query patterns, backup story, and read/write scaling.
questions.recommendation: Recommended: Postgres if coverage/overlap queries get complex; D1/SQLite for an edge-first, simpler model.

questions.title: How do team members authenticate, and is this single-org or multi-tenant?
questions.context: Auth + tenancy are deeply coupled to sessions and data isolation; changing later is weeks of work.
questions.consequence: Sets the sign-in UX, the row-level isolation model, and whether we need org invites from day one.

options.label: Managed auth, single org for now

questions.recommendation: Recommended: a managed provider with org/tenant support so we never roll our own credential storage.

questions.title: Where will this be deployed and run?
questions.context: The runtime target constrains the framework, cold-start budget, cron/alarm options, and ops model.
questions.consequence: Decides the build output, which runtime APIs we can use, and the deploy pipeline.

questions.title: Do multiple people edit the same schedule at once, and how should live updates propagate?
questions.context: A shared schedule is collaborative; the realtime choice affects conflict handling and infra.
questions.consequence: Decides between polling, WebSockets/Durable Objects, or SSE, and whether we need optimistic locking.
questions.recommendation: Recommended: a Durable Object per schedule with WebSocket fan-out if concurrent editing is real; polling if edits are rare.

questions.title: What shape should the API take for the client and any integrations?
questions.context: The API contract is a one-way door once external callers (mobile, integrations) depend on it.
questions.consequence: Sets versioning, the typed-client story, and how calendar integrations consume it.
questions.recommendation: Recommended: REST + OpenAPI so calendar integrations and a future mobile client can consume it.

questions.title: Which external calendars must we sync with, and in which direction?
questions.context: Two-way sync with Google/Microsoft is a major subsystem; knowing the scope prevents half-built sync.
questions.consequence: Determines OAuth scopes, webhook handling, and whether conflicts resolve locally or at the provider.

options.label: No external calendar sync in scope

questions.title: Is this paid, and if so what is the billing model?
questions.context: Billing shape (seat vs flat vs usage) picks the payment rail and changing it later is a one-way door.
questions.consequence: Decides Stripe Billing vs a simpler rail, the entitlement model, and whether seats gate features.

options.label: Free for now — no billing in v1

questions.recommendation: Recommended: defer billing out of v1 unless charging is the point; per-seat + Stripe Billing when it lands.

questions.title: What are the performance expectations (calendar render, availability query latency, team size)?
questions.context: Explicit targets prevent both under-building and premature optimization of the hot calendar view.
questions.consequence: Guides caching, the slot-query index strategy, and whether rendering needs virtualization.

questions.title: What accessibility bar must the calendar and booking flows meet?
questions.context: A date/time grid is notoriously hard for keyboard + screen-reader users; the bar must be set before building it.
questions.consequence: Decides keyboard-navigation design for the grid, focus management, and the axe/WCAG gate before ship.

options.label: WCAG 2.2 AA — keyboard grid + screen-reader + axe-clean

questions.recommendation: Recommended: WCAG 2.2 AA from the start — retrofitting a keyboard-navigable calendar grid is expensive.

questions.title: If AI suggests schedules or fills gaps, what must it never do without a human confirming?
questions.context: An AI that auto-assigns shifts touches people's real time; guardrails keep it trustworthy and on-brand.
questions.consequence: Defines which AI actions are auto vs confirmed, what gets logged, and the fallback when the model is unsure.
